Comment.MultiLanguageText: Caller-visible interface (C-115) - FC_ControlMain writes Mode/HopperHighLevel/limits/tunables in, reads Extend/Retract/RunPowerPack/fault bits out. See the block header for the Step/Mode value legend.
Latched jam hold, not a fault (C-123) - see the Pressure Detection network. Freezes ExtendDemand while set; clears itself once pressure has genuinely stayed clear for PressureClearResumeDelay.
Confirmed jams this cycle - reset each cycle start, not time-windowed. Compared against IO.PressureTripCountThreshold to raise Blocked.
ExtendDemand OR RetractDemand - the pump's own immediate (non-run-on) demand signal.
Cold-start guard for the pump run-on off-delay below - see that network's own comment.

AttributeList.Text: Pusher ram sequencing (C-118-C-125). Step legend (C-120): 0=Parked (idle/home, ram fully retracted, no motion) - 10=DriveToEndTravel (forward stroke in progress) - 20=Hold (paused at full travel, brief settle before retracting) - 30=Retract (returning to home; also the recovery/abort target from any bad state). Mode legend: 0=Off (finish a retract already in progress, then park; no new cycle starts) - 1=Auto (hopper-high-level starts a cycle) - 2=Manual (operator button/jog starts a cycle).
Enable
Both Limit Switches Active Simultaneously

HMI/DB_Settings times are Real seconds for operator legibility; every TON below needs its PT in DInt ms - one MUL+CONVERT pair per timer, matching the MotorDOL FTTime/EnableUPSTime idiom. Kept as one block up front rather than repeated at each timer, so the x1000 idiom is visibly consistent and only ever done once.
HMI Time Conversions

One function, one network: a trip must be debounced (PressureConfirmTimer) before it counts - momentary pressure spikes aren't a real jam. Hold latches through a confirmed trip and only releases once pressure has genuinely cleared for PressureClearResumeDelay, so a bouncing switch can't re-trigger the count on every scan. Count resets each cycle start (Step 0-to-10 launch condition), not on a rolling time window.
Pressure Trip Detection, Hold, And Counting
Blocked Fault (Too Many Jams)

Not-at-home while idle (power-up mid-stroke, or a cycle that ended without reaching HomeLimit) drives straight to Retract (30) to re-establish home before any new cycle is accepted - never straight back into a forward stroke from an unknown position. Suppressed during an active jog command so jogging isn't fought by an auto-retract.
Step 0 (Parked) - Transitions

Every abnormal exit - Off commanded mid-stroke, or a timeout, whether or not it also trips Blocked - goes straight to Retract (30), never a bare stop; the ram is never left sitting mid-travel. Only reaching FullTravelLimit cleanly goes to Hold (20) first, per the normal cycle.
Step 10 (Drive To End Travel) - Timer, Timeout Fault, And Transitions
Step 20 (Hold) - Timer And Transition

ParkedTimer's own Q only feeds the timeout fault, not a transition - if genuinely stuck retracting there's no safer step to force (unlike Step 10, nothing here can be aborted into); alarm-only by design, awaiting a human.
Step 30 (Retract) - Timer, Timeout Fault, And Transition
Jog Pre-Start Warning

PressureHold gates ExtendDemand so a confirmed jam holds the ram in place rather than continuing to push (a hold per C-123, not a fault - it clears and driving resumes the instant pressure has cleared). Jog demand only arms after JogPreStartTimer.Q so a jog button press always gets the same audible pre-start warning as an auto cycle, never an instant unwarned move.
Extend And Retract Demand
Pump Demand

Off-delay built from TON+inversion, not TOF/TONR (C-406). PumpEverDemanded guards a cold-start gap: on power-up PumpDemand and the timer's Q are both initially false, which would read as 'run-on already elapsed' and skip straight to no-run. RunPowerPack stays on through the run-on tail even after demand drops, but the Extend/Retract solenoids are not - they only ever follow live demand, gated by PowerPackRunningFB so the ram can't be commanded before the pump has confirmed running.
